question: What is forbidden for a married couple during intimacy?
answer:
With regards to what is forbidden in the Shari'ah, two things are explicitly forbidden; two things are forbidden directly in the texts of the Qur'an and Sunnah. And the first of these is anal intercourse. This is something that is absolutely forbidden without a doubt, according to the hadith. And we can infer it from the Qur'an; it is not explicit, but it has been derived from the Qur'an.

And as for the Qur'an implicitly, Allah says in the Qur'an, "Nisa'ukum harthun lakum fa'tu harthakum anna shi'tum": your women, your wives, are like a cultivation or like a field unto you, and therefore approach your wives however you wish to approach them. Now, the fact that Allah mentions a cultivation, our scholars have derived (in fact, even the tabi'un have derived) that the meaning therefore is that the cultivation occurs, obviously, from the vagina; it doesn't occur from the other organ. And therefore there is an indirect disapproval of anal intercourse.

As for the ahadith, there are numerous ahadith, reported by over seven Sahabah with over ten different chains, regarding this concept of forbidding anal intercourse. And in fact, this verse that I just quoted you, according to a number of authentic ahadith, was revealed because somebody asked the Prophet ﷺ about a certain issue of sex and sexuality, and this verse came down to respond to that.

And there are a number of hadith that forbid anal intercourse. Of them is the hadith in Abu Dawud that our Prophet ﷺ said: whoever comes to his wife while she is menstruating (that's the second prohibition; we'll talk about that), or from her back, meaning from her anus, has disbelieved in what has been revealed to the Prophet ﷺ. And in the other hadith, in Sunan an-Nasa'i, the Prophet said that Allah will not look at a man who approaches his wife from her back. Allah will not look at him, meaning Allah is angry at him; Allah is displeased with him.

And in Sunan an-Nasa'i as well, a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and he said, "O Messenger of Allah, may I engage in intercourse from behind?" That's the way that he phrased the question: from behind. So the Prophet said, "It is permissible." Then the man stood up to go back, and then he called him back and he said, "Wait, what did you mean when you said from behind?" Did you mean you're going to turn her around, meaning that her back is facing you, but from her front, her vagina? Or did you mean from her anus?

He literally asked; the Prophet ﷺ literally asked this: which of her orifices, which of her openings did you reference? Did you mean from her vagina but with her back facing you, meaning, of course, the sexual position that is different? Or did you mean from her adbar, from her dubur, meaning from her anus? Then the Prophet ﷺ said, "Inna Allaha la yastahyi min al-haqq": Allah is not embarrassed at speaking the truth. Do not approach women from their anuses. This is an explicit hadith in Sunan an-Nasa'i. And we mentioned here the verse as well: Allah says in the Qur'an that Allah is not embarrassed of the truth.

And there are also a number of narrations in this regard: that Umar ibn al-Khattab radiyallahu 'anhu came to the Prophet ﷺ and he said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have done something that will destroy me. I have done something that is going to destroy me." And the Prophet said, "What is this? What have you done?" So he said, "Last night I engaged in intercourse with my wife, but I turned her around." I turned her around, meaning that, again, the sexual position was that she was on her stomach, but he engaged in vaginal intercourse. And the Prophet allowed Umar; this is not a sin to do. In other words, sexual positions is something that is allowed, whichever position you want, but it is vaginal intercourse.

So the first thing that is completely forbidden is anal intercourse. There's no question about that.

The second that is completely forbidden as well, but to a lesser degree (it is still haram; both of them are haram, but there's degrees of haram), the second thing that is haram or sinful is to engage in intercourse during the period of the menses. During that timeframe, vaginal intercourse is not allowed.

Let me begin with the Qur'an. The Qur'an says, Surah Al-Baqarah verse 222: "They ask you about the menses. Say, it is something that is an irritation. So avoid approaching women during the time of their menses, and do not come close to them until they purify themselves." Once they have done the ghusl, then you may approach them from where Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala has allowed you. Ibn Abbas said "from where Allah has allowed you" means the vagina, not the anus. So again, this verse has also been used to indirectly forbid anal intercourse. But the Qur'an is very explicit about having intercourse during the menses.

And that is why there is unanimous consensus amongst all the scholars of Islam, without exception, that engaging in intercourse during the menses is a sinful act. And then the scholars differ: do you have to give a kaffarah? How much kaffarah, meaning expiation of money, monetary and whatnot? That's a secondary issue. And it is definitely good to give charity if that happens, and repent to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, and not do it again. It is something that should be avoided.

And Aisha radiyallahu 'anha reports that once, when her menses began, she was lying next to the Prophet ﷺ and she became embarrassed. This was early in the marriage. And so she left the bed and she wanted to sleep somewhere else. The Prophet ﷺ said, "What is the matter?" So she explained that she had begun her menses. So the Prophet ﷺ said, "Don't worry, put on another garment and then come next to me."

And of course the meaning here is that once the menses have begun, the lady does not become najis, which is something that some other faith traditions believe to this day. There are some faith traditions, including Orthodox Judaism as well, that when the lady is in her menses, her persona, her body, should not be touched, and anything she touches as well becomes impure. And in our Shari'ah, that is not the case. And so the Prophet ﷺ advised Aisha: don't worry about this, just protect the blood; we don't want the blood to come. And in those days they didn't have the type of menstrual pads that we do now. And so he advised her to put on another garment and then come back into bed.

And in another hadith, in Sahih Bukhari, a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and he asked, "O Messenger of Allah, what is permissible for me and my wife when she's in her menses?" He literally asked the question: what is halal? And the Prophet ﷺ said that you may do everything other than intercourse: "Isna'u kulla shay'in illa an-nikah." Everything is permissible: kissing and fondling and stimulation with the hands and with the other body parts; all of this is permissible. And anything that the two want to do, that they want to play around with between themselves, it is permissible, except for the actual vaginal intercourse. So the actual penetration is not allowed; anything other than this, it is allowed.

Now, some of the early scholars, they said that the man should avoid touching the woman's thighs or any area, even the groin area. And the reason for this, of course, is that they wanted the blood to not be touched. In our times, because there are menstrual pads, and because the area can be maintained in a better manner, the main point is that the man should avoid that blood. And if it does come on, then afterwards it can be washed off. But there should not be an intentional wanting to touch the blood, because obviously that blood is najas, and we don't willingly put najas onto our bodies.

Obviously, if it happens, it happens, and you just wash yourself. So realize that touching najasat is something that is discouraged, but in and of itself, if you have to do it, you have to do it. You change the diaper, or even when you cleanse yourself, I mean, you're touching najas, right? But you don't want to do that. And if it does happen, then you wash yourself off as soon as possible. So the correct opinion therefore, inshallah ta'ala, and this is the majority opinion, is that **everything is permissible during the menstrual cycle other than actual vaginal intercourse.**

Now, what else is forbidden? In reality, nothing else is forbidden, unless there's going to be a psychological harm, or unless another ruling of the Shari'ah is going to be contravened. And in our next question, I'll answer in more detail the one aspect of oral intercourse. I'll answer that in another video; you can see that, inshallah, in the next one.

But I want to now point out one thing: realize that sexual habits and sexual mores, they vary from time to place to society to culture. And I need you to pay attention to this: just because a certain society disdains a certain sexual practice does not make that practice haram. Understand this point. In human history, every society has developed its own mores and its own habits and its own mechanisms, if you like, of what is stimulating and whatnot within the bedroom. And the Shari'ah has not come to dictate cultures.

You may not like it, and that is your prerogative. Understand, you have a right, within your bedroom, to not do something that you think is inappropriate or whatnot. But don't bring religion into it and say it is haram just because your culture does not like it.

And the best example for this, actually, is that we have an authentic narration that demonstrates for us that between Makkah and Madinah there were sexual variations, and the Shari'ah adopted a neutral stance: hey, whatever you want to do is permissible. The Shari'ah came and did not prefer one over the other, and said, however you want to do it, that's between the two of you.

And the example here: Ibn Abbas narrates that the Ansar of Madinah used to live with the Jewish people, and the Ansar adopted the sexual habits of the Jews. And in Judaism to this day, Orthodox Judaism, no position is allowed other than the woman on her back, which is called the missionary position. No other position is allowed; you cannot have any other position. The woman has to be on her back, and there must be a sheet over the couple, and they have a lot of laws in this regard. So the Ansar, living with the Jews, they adopted that culture, because they viewed the Jews as being superior to them; they had knowledge of the Book.

And the Quraysh, Ibn Abbas said, they had no such qualms, and they would have intercourse from every position. The hadith actually says, Ibn Abbas says, that they would flip their women around, whichever position they wanted to. So they would engage in intercourse in every position they wanted to, whether it was on their backs, or whether it was turned around, or whether it was on their sides. This is in the hadith of Ibn Abbas.

So a muhajir man from Makkah married an Ansari lady from Madinah, and he attempted to engage in intercourse with her the way that he was accustomed to. I'm quoting you the hadith here, or the statement of Ibn Abbas. And the lady refused, and the lady said, "No, we can only have intercourse on our backs. That's what we are accustomed to." And the news spread amongst the people that there's a major marital dispute; the talk is now getting out because there's a marital problem happening, and they're wondering, well, who's right and who's wrong? And the news approached the Prophet ﷺ.

And so Allah 'azza wa jall revealed in the Qur'an the famous verse that I just mentioned to you: "Nisa'ukum harthun lakum fa'tu harthakum anna shi'tum." Your women are like a field unto you, so approach your women however you please. This is in the Qur'an: however you please. Allah is not dictating that there's a position that is haram or halal. No; however the two of you want to do this. And this means that, in essence, the man from Makkah basically was allowed to do whatever he wanted to do.

And the hadith of the Prophet was also very clear that you may approach your women while they're on their backs or while they're turned around, as long as you approach from the vagina, from the vaginal orifice. So one has to only take into account that anal intercourse is not allowed. As for sexual positions, whatever the couple wants to do, that is something that is permissible to them.

Now, there have been a lot of questions I've gotten about... Obviously, we're living at a time where, again, let's be honest here, brothers and sisters, the fetishes that are now prevalent... I'm getting all of these different questions, and subhanAllah, I don't want to go into detail here. Believe it or not, there should be some haya and whatnot in this regard. I'm just going to say generically: look, whatever is happening in the privacy of the bedroom that is not beyond the two things that are haram, which is anal intercourse (and anal intercourse literally means the penetration; that is what is haram) or intercourse during menses, anything other than this, if one wishes to engage in it with one's spouse, whether it's role-playing or using toys or anything of this nature...

A person can say, "I don't like it, I don't find it noble," and you know what, I sympathize with you 110%. But that's you and me, or that's some people. To say that it is sinful is different than to say that it is not noble. And I need us to understand this and differentiate it.

Look, I'll be the first to say that there is a problem of over-sexualization in the world that we live in. And because of this, it is affecting our marriages, and it is affecting our bedrooms as well, and it is affecting our sexual fetishes as well. If we were living in a pure environment where all of this was not around us, we would not be asking such questions. That is the truth. Still, what can we do? It's not our fault we're born into the time and place we're born into. It's not our fault we're aware of all that's going on. It's not our fault, at some level, that we're exposed to what we are exposed to. So yes, we are being affected. Yes, society around us is impacting us.

So we have to differentiate purity and nobility from haram and halal. Something might be ignoble, something might not be noble; it doesn't necessarily make it sinful in the eyes of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. And therefore I say that all of these personal things that a person might find pleasure in within a marriage, as long as no haram is being crossed (you're not doing zina with somebody you're not allowed to, you're not watching something you should not watch, and you are not doing the two things that we said are haram), it is best to be quiet, and the couple can decide what they want to do in this regard, and it is up to them. And there is no sin when it is in the privacy of one's bedroom.

However, I will make an exception for one thing, and I will say that that should be made haram, and that is the videotaping, even if it is done between the spouses. Why? Because, very simple: technically, theoretically (completely utopic theory, complete idealism), if the couple were to videotape and they themselves only watch it, perhaps one could make an argument that it is permissible for them to do. But let us now be real. Let us now get to the actual reality, the lived reality: these types of videos, Allah knows who is going to put their hands on them. It's very common for leakages to occur. It's very common for somebody else to see it.

And another point, which is very important: a marriage doesn't necessarily last forever, right? What if a divorce were to take place? How much are we seeing in the Western world, and even amongst Muslim couples as well, of people getting so angry that they release images that should not have been taken in the first place? So in that case, I will say, blanket-wise, that no: do not commit to imagery, do not make videos or pictures or whatnot of that which is inappropriate, because the reality is the potential harms are far, far greater than the potential things that might be beneficial.

And again, I have been asked this multiple times as well: if the couple is separated by physical distance, and they need to have that stimulation that's visual, can they engage in live phone calls that are just between the two of them? If it is something that is not recorded, and it is on a safe, direct line or whatnot, I can understand that that will bring some release, and some tension is going to be let out, perhaps, in that case. But to record it, really, this is highly problematic, because you do not know what's going to happen to that video in the future. So definitely I would say that that should not be done.

Other than that, inshallah ta'ala, everything is permissible between the two, as long as there's no long-term damage, or nothing that is actual haram that would be considered a sin to do. We will just be quiet about that and cover up what Allah has covered up. But it is between the two.

Now, by the way, before I finish this, one thing also needs to be said, to be very clear: this needs to be done by mutual consultation, meaning that the husband cannot force his wife to go above and beyond something that is the natural intercourse, and vice versa as well. So what Allah has mandated that each couple needs to do for the other is the basic intercourse, right? That is something that is there.

Now, if a particular partner has a bizarre fetish or kink or something of this nature, and the other partner does not, it is not fair to force the other partner. The other partner will say, "No, we will have the natural intercourse that Allah has allowed, what everybody does, and I don't want to do this particular thing; that's degrading to me," or whatnot. That's her right, or his right, to say that it is degrading, if it is something that is beyond normal, obviously, right? We're not talking about normal intercourse; that is what Allah has made mandatory between couples. They need to take care of each other in a manner that is halal.

So as long as it is done by mutual agreement, and no haram line is crossed, and those two things are not done, we will be quiet and let it go, as long as there's no, as we said, photography or video done, because that is a problem. And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala knows best.
